summary: Multiply the coefficients by d: the combination d·r of the v(x) has denominator 1 and size d·B, and normUnit(aC/d)·a·z is normalize(aC/d) ∈ {0, 1} times it.

steps.claim: Let z = ∑_x r(x)·(C·v(x)) with r supported in A, d·r(x) ∈ integralAway(n), and size ≤ B under p.

The coefficients d·r give an admissible combination z′ = ∑_x d·r(x)·v(x) of the v(x) with denominator 1 and size d·B under p. Let ζ = normalize(a·C/d), which is 1 if a·C ≠ 0 and 0 otherwise. Then normUnit(a·C/d)·a·z = ζ·z′: if a·C ≠ 0 the left side is (d/(aC))·a·C·∑ r(x) v(x) = z′, and if a·C = 0 both sides vanish. Since ζ is 0 or a root of unity, smul_of_eq_zero_or_isOfFinOrder gives the claim; the identity of the two sides is checked by simp and field_simp.
steps.lean:
convert smul_of_eq_zero_or_isOfFinOrder (ζ := normalize (a * C / d)) ⟨d • r,
    _, rfl⟩ _ using 1 <;> simp_all
    [sum_smul_index', ← mul_sum, hd.pos, or_iff_not_imp_left, normalize]; field_simp
